title: Tests after a tick bite (encephalitis, Lyme disease)
what: These tests show whether a tick passed on an infection. The tick itself and your blood can both be tested.
why: After a tick bite, especially if you were in an area with tick-borne encephalitis, or if you get a fever or redness.
duration: testing the tick usually takes 1 to 3 days; blood is not taken right away but at the time your doctor says
tell_doctor: When and where you were bitten
How long the tick was on your skin
If you had a tick-borne encephalitis vaccine
If you have a fever, headache, or a red patch

prepare.title: The tick
prepare.text: If the tick was removed, put it in a small jar with a damp cotton ball and close it tightly. Take it to the lab as soon as you can.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: Antibodies do not show up in the blood right away, usually only a few weeks after the bite. Your doctor will say when to give blood.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Better not to eat for 3 to 4 hours before the blood test. Water is fine.

bring: The tick in a closed jar, if you have it
steps: The tick is handed in to the lab and tested for infections
A band is tied above your elbow, and you are asked to clench your fist a few times
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick. Blood fills the tubes in a few seconds
A cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse, and they will help you lie down
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
For a month after the bite, watch for fever and check the bite site
Your doctor decides about preventive treatment. Do not put off the visit
red_flags: A red patch around the bite is getting bigger: see a doctor
Fever, severe headache, or body aches: see a doctor the same day
Confusion, seizures, or weakness in arms or legs: call emergency services

faq.q: How do I remove a tick the right way?
faq.a: Grab it close to the skin with tweezers or a thread, and slowly twist it out. Clean the spot with antiseptic.

faq.q: If the tick is clean, do I still need a blood test?
faq.a: Usually not, but your doctor decides. Watch how you feel for a month.

reminders.text: Tick bite tests tomorrow. Bring your vaccine records and write down the date of the bite.
